name: Open an account at a cooperative or ethical bank
shortDescription: Opening it is the fast part. Deciding to is the slow part.
longDescription: Cooperative and ethical banks are member-owned or mission-constrained, and most publish what they will and won't lend to. Opening an account is usually online and takes under half an hour — you don't have to move anything into it on day one.

name: Move your primary current account
shortDescription: Your everyday balance is working capital your bank lends out.
longDescription: This is the one that actually moves money rather than opening an option. Salary, direct debits and standing orders all have to follow — most European countries mandate a switching service that does this within days and forwards anything missed. Worth checking in on, because the old account tends to linger.

name: Move your savings to an ethical bank
shortDescription: Savings are the easiest balance to move — nothing is attached to them.
longDescription: Unlike a current account, savings have no direct debits or salary to redirect, so moving them is a transfer and nothing else. It's the largest amount most people can redirect in a single afternoon.

name: Move your money out of a detention or fossil financier
shortDescription: Check the lists first, then decide whether your bank is on one.
longDescription: BankTrack and Urgewald publish researched, sourced lists of which banks finance fossil expansion, arms and private detention. Look your bank up. If it's there, moving is a concrete response — and telling them why is the next action.

name: Switch your card to a non-US-linked issuer
shortDescription: Every card transaction routes a fee to a network.
longDescription: Visa and Mastercard take an interchange fee on essentially every card payment in Europe. A domestic debit scheme or a card issued on a European network keeps that fee inside the local system.

name: Pay by Wero, girocard, Bizum or your domestic scheme
shortDescription: Most European countries have their own rails. Use them.
longDescription: Domestic account-to-account schemes settle directly between banks and don't route a fee through a US card network. Making one your default for everyday payments is a per-transaction redirect that adds up faster than any single switch.

name: Move one recurring bill to SEPA direct transfer
shortDescription: Same bill, no card network in the middle.
longDescription: Most utilities, insurers and telecoms accept SEPA direct debit or standing order as an alternative to paying by card. Switching one recurring bill removes a card fee permanently.

name: Stop using PayPal for one recurring payment
shortDescription: An extra US intermediary on a payment that doesn't need one.
longDescription: PayPal sits between you and the merchant and takes a cut of each transaction. Most merchants accept SEPA direct debit or a domestic scheme instead — changing the payment method on one recurring charge takes a couple of minutes.

name: Remove Apple Pay or Google Pay as your default
shortDescription: A wallet layer on top of the card fee you're already paying.
longDescription: Tokenised wallets add a platform fee on top of card interchange and give the platform a view of your purchase history. Removing the default takes one settings change; your physical card and domestic scheme still work.

name: Cancel a US-issued credit card
shortDescription: Close the line, not just the habit.
longDescription: An unused card still represents a lending relationship and often an annual fee. Clear the balance, redirect anything recurring on it first, then close it in writing so there's a record.

name: Pay cash for a week
shortDescription: No interchange, no data, no intermediary.
longDescription: Cash is the only payment method that routes nothing to anyone. A week of it also makes visible how many small transactions were going through a card network without you noticing.

name: Tell your bank why you left, in writing
shortDescription: A closed account is a number. A letter is a reason.
longDescription: Banks track attrition but not motive unless you supply it. A short written note at closure — naming what you objected to — puts a reason on the file that retention teams actually read and report upward.

name: Ask your club or congregation which bank it uses
shortDescription: Organisations hold larger balances than any of their members.
longDescription: A sports club, choir, Verein or congregation has a treasurer, a bank account and usually nobody who has ever asked about it. The question alone often starts the first review that account has had in a decade.
